mainTopic: Praise of the righteous in תהלים פרק א and advice on how to learn Torah well
overview: This amud praises the person described in the opening פסוקים of תהלים and gives advice on how to learn Torah. First, תהלים 1:1 is read as praise of אברהם אבינו, who refused to join the דור הפלגה, סדום, and the scoffing פלשתים. A side discussion explains 'אשרי איש ירא את ה׳': רב says it means doing תשובה while still strong, and רבי יהושע בן לוי says it means beating the יצר like a man. רבי אלעזר adds that one should love the מצוות themselves, not their reward. Back in תהלים 1:2, רבי teaches that a person truly learns only the Torah his heart desires, illustrated by a story with לוי. רבא and others then give a string of lessons: Torah becomes the learner's own, first learn broadly and then analyze, keep reviewing even if you forget, grow from private learning to honor and teaching, gather Torah little by little, and secure what you learn like a hunter who keeps his catch. Finally, the school of רבי ינאי says learning from only one teacher brings no blessing. רב חסדא limits this to סברא, explaining on the next amud why גמרא is better learned from one teacher.

steps.title: אברהם did not follow the counsel of the Tower-builders
steps.stepSummary: The first part of תהלים 1:1, 'who did not walk in the counsel of the wicked', is read as describing אברהם אבינו, who did not join the דור הפלגה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The man in the פסוק is אברהם אבינו. He did not walk in the counsel of the דור הפלגה, who were wicked, as it says: 'Come, let us build us a city.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of explaining תהלים 1:1 phrase by phrase. Here it says the 'counsel of the wicked' that the happy man avoided was the plan of the דור הפלגה, and that man was אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each part of the פסוק is tied to a real group that אברהם refused to join. The proof that the דור הפלגה were 'רשעים' is their own plan to build a city and tower, quoted from בראשית.

keyTerms.meaning: The generation of the dispersion, who built the Tower of Bavel

phrases.english: Our forefather Abraham,
phrases.notes: This picks up a drasha from just before: the happy man of תהלים 1:1 is אברהם.

phrases.english: who did not walk in the counsel of
the people of the generation of the dispersion,
who were wicked,
as it is stated: “Come, let us build us a city.”
phrases.notes: בראשית 11:4

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a drasha on תהלים 1:1 that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'לא הלך בעצת רשעים' means אברהם did not join the plans of the דור הפלגה.

steps.title: אברהם did not stand with the sinners of סדום
steps.stepSummary: 'Nor stood in the way of sinners' is read as אברהם not joining the people of סדום, whom the תורה calls חטאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Nor stood in the way of sinners' means he did not take the stand of סדום, who were sinners, as it says: 'The men of סדום were wicked and sinners to ה׳ exceedingly.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second part of the same פסוק. It explains 'the way of sinners' as the people of סדום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'חטאים' in תהלים is matched to the same word used about סדום in בראשית. That shared word is how the גמרא knows which group the פסוק means.

phrases.english: “Nor stood in the way of sinners”:
phrases.notes: תהלים 1:1

phrases.english: that he did not stand in the stand of Sodom,
who were sinners,
as it is stated: “Now the men of Sodom
were wicked and sinners against the Lord exceedingly.”
phrases.notes: בראשית 13:13

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next phrase of the same פסוק, still about אברהם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'ובדרך חטאים לא עמד' means אברהם did not side with סדום.

steps.title: אברהם did not sit with the scoffing פלשתים
steps.stepSummary: 'Nor sat in the seat of the scornful' is read as אברהם not sitting among the פלשתים, who were scoffers, proven from how they mocked שמשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Nor sat in the seat of scoffers' means he did not sit among the פלשתים, because they were scoffers, as it says: 'When their hearts were merry, they said: Call for שמשון so he can entertain us.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third and last part of the פסוק. The 'seat of scoffers' is the company of the פלשתים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof that the פלשתים were scoffers comes from a much later story, when they mocked the captured שמשון for fun. That later behavior shows what kind of people they were.
steps.whatToRemember: All three parts of תהלים 1:1 (walking, standing, sitting) describe groups אברהם refused to join: the דור הפלגה, סדום, and the פלשתים.

phrases.english: “Nor sat in the seat of the scornful”:
that he did not sit in the seat of the Philistines,
because they were scoffers,
as it is stated: “And it came to pass, when their hearts were merry,
that they said: Call for Samson, that he may make us sport.”
phrases.notes: שופטים 16:25

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the three-part reading of תהלים 1:1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'ובמושב לצים לא ישב' means אברהם did not sit among the scoffing פלשתים.

steps.title: Why does the verse praise only a man?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'אשרי איש ירא את ה׳' and asks whether it means only a man is praised and not a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Happy is the man who fears ה׳.' Does that mean happy is a man, but not a woman?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new, similar פסוק and asks about one word in it. This question sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fearing ה׳ applies to everyone, so the word 'איש' seems unneeded or even limiting. The גמרא expects that word to teach something extra.

phrases.english: “Happy is the man that fears the Lord”:
phrases.notes: תהלים 112:1

phrases.english: Happy is a man, and not happy is a woman?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from תהלים פרק א to a similar 'אשרי' פסוק in תהלים קיב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word 'איש' adds, since the פסוק surely does not exclude women.

steps.title: רב: happy is one who repents while still strong
steps.stepSummary: רב, quoted by רב עמרם, says 'איש' means doing תשובה while one is still a vigorous man, before old age.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם said in the name of רב: Happy is the one who does תשובה while he is still an 'איש'.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first answer to the question. 'איש' is not about men versus women. It describes the time of life when a person repents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repenting while you still have strength and desire is worth more than repenting once old age has made sin hard anyway. So 'איש' praises the timing of the תשובה.

phrases.english: Rav Amram said that Rav said:
Happy is one who does repentance
while he is still “a man.”
phrases.notes: He means while still in his strong years, before he grows old and weak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'איש' describes a stage of life: doing תשובה while still young and strong.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: beat your inclination like a man
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives a second answer: 'איש' describes the strength with which one overcomes the יצר הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Happy is the one who overpowers his יצר like a man.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer to the same question. Here 'איש' describes how a person fights his יצר, with strength like a strong man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again 'איש' does not leave out women. For רב it points to when one repents. For רבי יהושע בן לוי it points to the strong, determined way one beats the יצר.
steps.whatToRemember: Both answers agree that 'איש' praises a quality, not gender: רב says repenting while strong, רבי יהושע בן לוי says fighting the יצר with strength.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Happy is one who triumphs
over his inclination “like a man.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the same question that רב answered.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'איש' describes manly strength in overcoming the יצר.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: loving the מצוות themselves, not their reward
steps.stepSummary: On the rest of the פסוק, 'במצותיו חפץ מאד', רבי אלעזר says the person delights in the מצוות themselves, not in the reward they bring.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He delights greatly in His מצוות.' רבי אלעזר said: in His מצוות, and not in the reward for His מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues with the next words of the same פסוק. רבי אלעזר reads them carefully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have praised someone who wants the reward of מצוות. Because it says 'במצותיו', רבי אלעזר learns that the praise is for loving the מצוות for their own sake.

phrases.english: “He delights greatly in His מצוות”:
Rabbi Elazar said:
“In His מצוות,” and not in the reward of His מצוות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second half of the same פסוק discussed in steps 4 to 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The praised person loves the מצוות themselves, not their reward.

steps.title: Support from אבות: serve without expecting reward
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי אלעזר's idea matches the משנה in אבות: be like servants who serve their master without expecting a reward.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what we learned in a משנה: He used to say: Do not be like servants who serve the master in order to get a reward. Instead, be like servants who serve the master not in order to get a reward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי אלעזר's reading fits an older teaching in a משנה. That gives his idea support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'והיינו דתנן' means 'this is the same as what the משנה taught.' The servant who serves for no pay is the person who loves 'מצותיו' and not 'שכר מצותיו'.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what we learned in a משנה
On condition that, in order to

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר's lesson, supported by the משנה in אבות: the ideal is to serve ה׳ for the sake of the מצוות themselves, not for the reward.
steps.confusionAlert: 'הרב' here means the master of the servants, not a rabbi.

phrases.english: And this is what we learned:
He used to say:
phrases.notes: 'He' is אנטיגנוס איש סוכו, in אבות 1:3.

phrases.english: Do not be like servants
who serve the master
on the condition of receiving a reward;
rather, be like servants
who serve the master
not on the condition of receiving a reward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אלעזר's reading with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's reading that one should delight in the מצוות and not their reward.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in אבות 1:3, the saying of אנטיגנוס איש סוכו about serving without expecting reward.

steps.title: Learn Torah in the area your heart desires
steps.stepSummary: רבי reads 'his delight is in the Torah of ה׳' to mean that a person only truly learns the part of Torah his heart wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: "But his delight is in the Torah of ה׳." רבי said: A person only learns Torah from a place his heart desires, as it says: "But his delight is in the Torah of ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the side discussion of תהלים 112:1 and returns to תהלים פרק א, now to פסוק 2. It brings רבי's lesson: real learning happens in the part of Torah you are excited about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 1-3 explained תהלים 1:1, and steps 4-8 were a side discussion of a similar פסוק in תהלים קיב. Now the גמרא is back in תהלים פרק א, and רבי reads 'חֶפְצוֹ' (his delight) as telling us what to learn. The Torah a person learns well is the Torah he actually wants to learn.

keyTerms.meaning: From the place (area of Torah) his heart desires

phrases.english: "But his delight is in the Torah of the Lord,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 1:2

phrases.english: Rabbi said:
phrases.notes: Just 'רבי' with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: A person does not learn Torah
except from a place that his heart desires,
as it is said: "But his delight is in the Torah of the Lord."

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אִם בְּתוֹרַת ה׳ חֶפְצוֹ, אָמַר רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side discussion of תהלים 112:1 (steps 4–8) to the reading of תהלים פרק א, now פסוק 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person truly learns Torah only in the area his heart desires.

steps.title: The story of choosing between משלי and תהלים
steps.stepSummary: לוי and רבי שמעון ברבי finish a book and disagree about what to learn next; תהלים is chosen, and when they reach this פסוק, רבי teaches his lesson.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי and רבי שמעון ברבי were sitting before רבי, learning a section. When they finished the book, לוי said: Let them bring us משלי. רבי שמעון ברבי said: Let them bring us תהלים. He overruled לוי and they brought תהלים. When they reached "But his delight is in the Torah of ה׳," רבי explained: A person only learns Torah from a place his heart desires.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story where רבי first said this teaching. It sets up לוי's clever reply in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is that לוי wanted משלי but was outvoted, so they learned תהלים against his wishes. Then the very פסוק they reached says you should learn what your heart wants. That is what makes the next line funny.

keyTerms.meaning: Were learning through a section of the text

phrases.english: Levi and Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi,
were sitting before Rabbi,
and they were learning the section.
The book was finished,
Levi said: Let them bring [us] Proverbs,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is the corrected wording; either way, the meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi, said:
Let them bring [us] Psalms.
He overruled Levi
and they brought Psalms.
When they reached here:
"But his delight is in the Torah of the Lord,"
Rabbi explained and said:
A person does not learn Torah
except from a place that his heart desires.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵוִי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי יָתְבִי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the story where רבי's teaching from step 9 was first said.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי taught his lesson while his students were learning תהלים, a book לוי had not wanted to learn.

steps.title: לוי's witty reply: you have let me leave
steps.stepSummary: לוי uses רבי's own teaching to say he may now get up, since his heart wanted משלי, not תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי said: רבי, you have given us permission to stand up.
steps.whatsHappening: לוי answers רבי with a clever line that ends the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person only learns where his heart desires, then לוי, who wanted משלי, gains nothing by staying for תהלים. So he jokingly says רבי's own words let him get up and go.

phrases.english: Levi said: My teacher,
you have given us permission to stand up.
phrases.notes: He means himself: since his heart wanted משלי, by רבי's own rule he may get up and leave.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵוִי: רַבִּי, נָתַתָּ לָנוּ רְשׁוּת לַעֲמוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: לוי applies רבי's teaching from step 10 to his own situation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By רבי's own rule, someone made to learn what he did not choose may get up and leave.

steps.title: God fulfills the wishes of one who learns Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבדימי בר חמא reads the פסוק differently: whoever is busy with Torah, God grants his desires.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבדימי בר חמא said: Whoever is busy with Torah, הקדוש ברוך הוא does what he desires, as it says: "But in the Torah of ה׳ is his delight."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, different reading of the same words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, 'his delight' was about which Torah a person chooses to learn. For רבי אבדימי בר חמא, 'his delight' means the person's wishes, which come true through Torah learning. Same words, a new idea.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is busy with Torah learning
The Holy One, Blessed be He

phrases.english: Rabbi Avdimi bar Ḥama said:
Anyone who is busy with Torah,

phrases.aramaic: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹשֶׂה לוֹ חֲפָצָיו,
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, does his desires for him,
as it is said: "But in the Torah of the Lord is his desire."
phrases.notes: He reads it as: through the Torah of ה׳, the person's desire is fulfilled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבְדִּימִי בַּר חָמָא: כׇּל הָעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the same פסוק that רבי explained in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God fulfills the wishes of one who is busy with Torah.

steps.title: רבא: always learn where your heart desires
steps.stepSummary: רבא agrees with רבי's reading: a person should always learn the Torah his heart desires.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A person should always learn Torah in a place his heart desires, as it says: "But his delight is in the Torah of ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא repeats רבי's idea, this time as advice for how a person should learn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי said a person only learns in the area his heart wants, which describes how learning works. רבא turns this into guidance: 'לְעוֹלָם', always choose to learn what you desire.

phrases.english: Rava said:
A person should always learn Torah
in a place that his heart desires,
as it is said: "But his delight is in the Torah of the Lord."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לְעוֹלָם יִלְמוֹד אָדָם תּוֹרָה בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁלִּבּוֹ חָפֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי אבדימי's different reading, רבא goes back to רבי's reading from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should always learn the Torah his heart desires.

steps.title: The Torah becomes the learner's own
steps.stepSummary: רבא notes the פסוק first says 'the Torah of ה׳' and then 'his Torah', teaching that Torah becomes called by the learner's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: At first it is called by the name of הקדוש ברוך הוא, and in the end it is called by his name, as it says: "In the Torah of ה׳ is his delight," and then "and in his Torah he meditates day and night."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא makes a second point from the same פסוק, about the change in wording from 'Torah of ה׳' to 'his Torah'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the פסוק calls it 'the Torah of ה׳'. The second half calls it 'his Torah', meaning the learner's. רבא learns that by toiling in Torah, a person comes to own it, so it is called by his name.

keyTerms.meaning: It is called by his name

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק "כִּי אִם בְּתוֹרַת ה׳ חֶפְצוֹ" is read three ways: learn what your heart desires (רבי and רבא), God fulfills the learner's wishes (רבי אבדימי בר חמא), and Torah starts as God's and becomes the learner's own (רבא).
steps.confusionAlert: In 'וּלְבַסּוֹף נִקְרֵאת עַל שְׁמוֹ', 'his name' is not God's name; it means the name of the person learning.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
At first it is called by the name
of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
and in the end it is called by his name,
phrases.notes: 'His name' here means the name of the person who learns it.

phrases.english: as it is said: "In the Torah of the Lord is his delight,"
"and in his Torah he meditates day and night."
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the same פסוק, תהלים 1:2. Now it says 'his Torah' instead of 'the Torah of ה׳'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: בַּתְּחִילָּה נִקְרֵאת עַל שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא adds a second teaching on the same פסוק, now based on the change in its wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah is first called God's Torah, but through learning it becomes called the learner's own Torah.

steps.title: First learn, then analyze
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from the order of the פסוק that a person should first learn Torah broadly and only afterward analyze it in depth.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: A person should always learn Torah first, and only afterward think it through deeply. This is because the פסוק first says "in the Torah of ה׳" and only then says "and in his Torah he meditates."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives another lesson from the same פסוק in תהלים, this time from the order of its two halves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half, "בְּתוֹרַת ה׳", describes plain learning. The second half, "יֶהְגֶּה", describes deep thinking. Since the plain learning comes first in the פסוק, רבא says a person should build basic knowledge first and only then go deep.

keyTerms.meaning: He should think it over and analyze it deeply

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a basic order for learning: get a broad picture before digging into fine analysis.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רָבָא: לְעוֹלָם יִלְמַד אָדָם תּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: And Rava said: A person should always learn Torah,
and afterward he should analyze it,
as it is said: "In the Torah of the Lord,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 1:2

phrases.english: and afterward: "And in his Torah he meditates."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: לְעוֹלָם יִלְמַד אָדָם תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third lesson רבא draws from the same פסוק, this time from the order of its two halves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Broad learning comes first; deep analysis comes after.

steps.title: Keep reviewing even if you forget or don't understand
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that a person should keep reviewing Torah even if he forgets it or doesn't understand it, learning this from the word "גָּרְסָה" (crushed) instead of "טָחֲנָה" (ground fine).
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: A person should always keep going over his learning, even if he will forget it, and even if he doesn't understand what it is saying. The פסוק says "My soul crushes with longing." It says "crushes," not "grinds."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא encourages a learner to keep reviewing and saying the words of Torah, even when he forgets or doesn't fully understand them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Crushing breaks something into rough pieces. Grinding makes it into fine powder. The פסוק uses "crushing" to show that rough, basic learning is already something the soul longs for, even without full, fine understanding.

keyTerms.meaning: He should review or recite his learning

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying understanding doesn't matter. He is saying that not understanding yet is no reason to stop learning.
steps.whatToRemember: Never stop learning just because you forget or don't fully understand. Rough, basic learning has real value.

phrases.english: And Rava said: A person should always review his learning,
phrases.notes: The word for reviewing here comes from the same root as "גָּרְסָה" in the פסוק below, which means crushing.

phrases.english: even though he forgets,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא יָדַע מַאי קָאָמַר,
phrases.english: and even though he does not know what it is saying,
as it is said: "My soul crushes with longing,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 119:20

phrases.english: "Crushes" is written, and "grinds" is not written.
phrases.notes: Grinding into fine powder stands for deep, full understanding. The פסוק only asks for rough crushing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another of רבא's teachings on Torah study. It moves from the order of learning to why we keep reviewing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Keep reviewing Torah even when you forget it or don't understand it.

steps.title: Upon the heights, or on a seat?
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out two פסוקים in משלי that seem to clash: one places the Torah's call "upon the heights" and the other "on a seat."
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא pointed out a contradiction: One פסוק says "upon the heights," and another פסוק says "on a seat."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא sets up a contradiction between two פסוקים. His answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים describe where the Torah's call is found, but they describe it differently. "Upon the heights" sounds like standing in an unsettled place, while "on a seat" sounds like being settled and honored. רבא asks which one is true.

keyTerms.meaning: Points out a contradiction between two sources

phrases.english: Rava pointed out a contradiction: It is written "upon the heights,"
phrases.notes: משלי 9:3

phrases.english: and it is written "on a seat"!
phrases.notes: משלי 9:14

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא רָמֵי: כְּתִיב ״עַל גַּפֵּי״, וּכְתִיב ״עַל כִּסֵּא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא moves from the פסוק in תהלים to a new pair of פסוקים in משלי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two descriptions of where the Torah's call is placed, in משלי 9:3 and 9:14
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק describes an unsettled high place and the other a settled seat, so they seem to clash.

steps.title: First on the heights, later on a seat
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that both פסוקים are true at different stages: a learner starts out unsettled and later earns a seat of honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first, "upon the heights"; and in the end, "on a seat."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own contradiction by saying each פסוק describes a different stage in a learner's life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two פסוקים do not argue with each other; they describe a path over time. A beginner has no settled place yet, but as he grows in Torah he is given a seat of honor.

keyTerms.meaning: On a seat, meaning a settled place of honor

phrases.english: At first, "upon the heights,"
and in the end, "on a seat."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different stages in time: each פסוק describes a different point in the learner's growth
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים seemed to give conflicting descriptions.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are true: the unsettled heights come at the start, and the seat of honor comes in the end.

steps.title: On the high places, or by the path?
steps.stepSummary: A second contradiction: one phrase places the Torah "on the top of high places" and the next says "by the path."
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written "on the top of high places," and it is written "by the path."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a second contradiction of the same kind. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A high, hidden spot and a public road are opposite kinds of places. So where is the Torah found: up high and apart, or out where everyone passes?

keyTerms.meaning: On the top of high places
By the path; along the road

phrases.english: It is written "on the top of high places,"
phrases.notes: משלי 8:2. Both phrases come from this same פסוק.

phrases.english: and it is written "by the path."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second contradiction built the same way as step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two descriptions of the Torah's place in משלי 8:2
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A high, private spot and a public road are opposites, so the two phrases seem to clash.

steps.title: First in private, later in public
steps.stepSummary: The answer follows the same pattern: a learner first studies privately up on the heights, and in the end spreads Torah out on the public path.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first, "on the top of high places"; and in the end, "by the path."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers this contradiction the same way as the first one: each phrase describes a different stage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first a person learns apart, in a high, private place. Later, once he has grown, his Torah reaches the public road, where he teaches others. Both contradictions describe the same idea of growth over time.

keyTerms.meaning: High places, here a private spot apart from people
A road, meaning the public space where people pass

steps.whatToRemember: Both contradictions are solved the same way, "at first... in the end": a Torah learner starts humble and private, and grows into honor and public teaching.

phrases.english: At first, "on the top of high places,"
and in the end, "by the path."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction in step 19, using the same "at first / in the end" pattern as step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different stages in time: private learning at first, public teaching later
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Torah seemed to be described as both hidden away and out in public.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is both, at different stages: private study at the start, public teaching in the end.

steps.title: עולא's contradiction: cistern or well?
steps.stepSummary: עולא notes that one פסוק first speaks of drinking from a cistern, and then of water flowing from a well.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא raised a contradiction: It says 'Drink water from your cistern,' and it also says 'and flowing water from within your well.'
steps.whatsHappening: עולא raises a new contradiction, in the same style as רבא's earlier ones. A cistern only holds water that is poured into it, but a well makes its own flowing water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two halves of the פסוק seem to describe two different sources of water. Is the learner a cistern that only collects, or a well that gushes out? The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He raises a contradiction (literally 'throws' two sources against each other)
Cistern: a pit that collects and holds water
Well: a spring that produces its own water

phrases.english: Ulla raised a contradiction:
It is written: "Drink water from your cistern,"
phrases.notes: משלי 5:15

phrases.english: and it is written: "and flowing water from within your well."
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the same פסוק. A cistern just holds water; a well bubbles up with its own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third contradiction in the same series, this time raised by עולא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A cistern only holds collected water, while a well produces its own, so the פסוק seems to describe the learner in two opposite ways.

steps.title: First collect, later flow
steps.stepSummary: Both halves are true at different stages: at first a learner collects like a cistern, and in the end he flows like a well.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first, 'drink from your cistern,' and in the end, 'flowing water from within your well.'
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers his contradiction with the same 'beginning and end' pattern used in steps 18 and 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the start a learner only takes in what his teachers give him, like a cistern holding water poured into it. Later he becomes like a well, producing fresh Torah of his own. Both halves describe the same person at different stages of growth.
steps.whatToRemember: Three contradictions in a row (steps 17, 19, 21) are all solved the same way: the פסוקים describe a learner at the beginning and at the end of his growth.

phrases.english: At first: "drink from your cistern,"
and in the end: "flowing water from within your well."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 21
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different time periods: the two halves describe two stages in a learner's life
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seems to describe the learner in two conflicting ways at once
steps.terutzMaskana: First he absorbs his teachers' Torah like a cistern; later he produces his own like a flowing well

steps.title: Gather Torah little by little
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that Torah learned in big bundles shrinks, while Torah gathered little by little grows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב סחורה, in the name of רב הונא: What does the פסוק mean, 'Wealth from vanity will dwindle, but one who gathers little by little will increase'? If a person makes his Torah into big bundles, it dwindles; if he gathers it little by little, it grows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about how to learn. רב הונא explains a פסוק in משלי as advice about the pace of learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מהבל (from vanity) is read like חבילות (bundles). Grabbing huge amounts at once without review makes Torah shrink. Building slowly, a little at a time, makes it grow.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written: opens an explanation of a פסוק
Bundles: large heaps taken all at once

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב סְחוֹרָה אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Sechora said that Rav Huna said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"Wealth from vanity will dwindle,
phrases.notes: משלי 13:11. Here מהבל is read as if it said חבילות, bundles.

phrases.english: but one who gathers little by little will increase"?
If a person makes his Torah
into big bundles, it dwindles;
but if he gathers little by little, it will grow.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב סְחוֹרָה אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching on how to learn Torah, still drawn from משלי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah learned in big bundles shrinks; Torah gathered slowly, a little at a time, increases.

steps.title: רבא: the Sages know this but don't do it
steps.stepSummary: רבא comments that the רבנן know this advice and yet fail to follow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The רבנן know this thing, and yet they go against it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a sharp remark about רב הונא's advice. Even scholars who know they should learn slowly don't actually do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the rule itself. רבא points out the gap between knowing good advice and living by it, which sets up רב נחמן בר יצחק's response in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They go against it, they fail to follow it

phrases.english: Rava said:
The Sages know this thing,
phrases.notes: "This thing" means the advice just given in step 23: gather Torah little by little.

phrases.english: and they go against it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: יָדְעִי רַבָּנַן לְהָא מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on how people actually treat the advice of step 23
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scholars know they should learn slowly and review, but they don't actually do it.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: I did it, and it worked
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק testifies that he followed the advice and his learning stayed with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: I did it, and my learning lasted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers רבא's remark with his own experience. He followed the 'little by little' method, and it really worked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said scholars don't follow the advice. רב נחמן בר יצחק shows that it can be done, and his own lasting learning is living proof that רב הונא's teaching is true.

keyTerms.meaning: It lasted with me, it stayed in my hands

steps.whatToRemember: Learning slowly and reviewing is not just theory. רב נחמן בר יצחק did it, and his Torah lasted.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
I did it,
and it stayed with me.
phrases.notes: Literally "it lasted in my hands". He means the Torah he learned this way stayed with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: אֲנָא עֲבִידְתַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבא's remark in step 24 with personal testimony
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's teaching that Torah gathered little by little lasts
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן בר יצחק's own experience: he learned this way and his learning lasted

steps.title: The deceitful hunter will not live long
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה reads יחרך as 'will not live and will not lengthen days', teaching that the deceitful hunter will not live long.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שיזבי said in the name of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: What does the פסוק mean, 'The deceitful one will not roast his catch'? The deceitful hunter will not live and will not have long days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another explanation of a פסוק from משלי. The rare word יחרך is read as a combination of two words: יחיה (he will live) and יאריך (he will lengthen).
steps.deeperAnalysis: By splitting up יחרך, the פסוק is read as a warning: the deceitful hunter will not live a long life. Coming right after the teachings about slow, careful learning, it fits the same theme of how to learn properly.

keyTerms.meaning: Will roast; here read as יִחְיֶה + יַאֲרִיךְ

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁיזְבִי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה:
phrases.english: Rav Sheizvi said in the name of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"The deceitful one will not roast his catch"?
phrases.notes: משלי 12:27

phrases.english: He will not live and will not have long days,
phrases.notes: The word יחרך is split into two: יחיה (live) and יאריך (lengthen).

phrases.english: the deceitful hunter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁיזְבִי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another explanation of a פסוק in משלי, placed in the series of teachings about learning Torah
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reading יחרך as יחיה and יאריך: the deceitful hunter will not live a long life.

steps.title: רב ששת: the clever hunter roasts his catch
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת reads the פסוק as praise: the clever hunter makes sure he keeps what he caught.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת said: the cunning hunter will roast (his catch).
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives a second reading of the same פסוק that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה just explained. He reads it in the opposite direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה read יחרוך as a punishment: the deceitful hunter will not live long. רב ששת reads הרמאי as 'the clever one' and יחרוך as 'he roasts.' A smart hunter secures his catch so it cannot escape. In learning, that means a wise student makes sure his learning stays with him.
steps.confusionAlert: Here הרמאי is not 'the cheater.' For רב ששת it means the clever one, so this reading is praise, not criticism.

phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet said:
"The cunning hunter will roast (his catch)."
phrases.notes: This is the same פסוק from משלי that the previous step explained, now read in a positive way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a reading of the פסוק that is the opposite of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The clever hunter secures his catch. In the same way, a wise learner makes sure he keeps what he learned.

steps.title: רב דימי's parable of the bird catcher
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי compares this to a bird catcher who breaks the wings of each bird so that none escape.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: this is like a man catching birds. If he breaks the wings of the first one, all of them stay with him. If not, they do not stay with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי gives a parable that explains רב ששת's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the hunter lets the first bird fly off while he chases the next one, he ends up with nothing. Learning works the same way: if you do not lock in what you already learned before moving on, it slips away. Securing each piece as you go keeps all of it.

keyTerms.meaning: when he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
they stay in his hand; he keeps them

steps.whatToRemember: Secure each piece of learning before moving on, or everything flies away.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
It is comparable to a person who hunts birds.
If he breaks the wings of the first one,
all of them remain in his hand;
and if not, they do not remain in his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רב ששת's reading with a parable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: You keep everything you caught only if you secure each catch before taking the next.

steps.title: A replanted tree: learn from more than one teacher
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ינאי learns from the word שתול (replanted) that someone who learns from only one רב never sees blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he shall be like a tree planted by streams of water.' The school of רבי ינאי said: it says 'a tree שתול' (replanted) and not 'a tree נטוע' (planted). Anyone who learns Torah from only one teacher never sees a sign of blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the opening פסוקים of תהלים and quotes the school of רבי ינאי on the word שתול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נטוע is a tree planted and left in one spot. שתול is a tree moved and replanted somewhere else. The פסוק chose שתול, which teaches that a תלמיד חכם should move between teachers and not stay with only one.

keyTerms.meaning: replanted, moved from one place to another
planted and staying in one place

phrases.english: "And he shall be like a tree planted by streams of water."
phrases.notes: תהלים 1:3

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai say:
"Like a replanted tree" and not "like a planted tree":
anyone who learns Torah from one teacher
never sees a sign of blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the hunter discussion and returns to the explanation of תהלים chapter 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning Torah from only one רב does not bring blessing.

steps.title: רב חסדא's students leave him for רבא
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says he is afraid to share this teaching because his students will leave him. He shares it, and they leave for רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to the רבנן: I want to tell you something, but I am afraid you will leave me and go. Anyone who learns Torah from one teacher never sees a sign of blessing. They left him and went to רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short story showing what happened when רב חסדא taught this rule. It also sets up his next statement, which limits the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's fear came true. His students took the rule literally and went to learn from another teacher. This leads him to explain exactly when the rule applies.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to the Rabbis:
I want to tell you something,
but I am afraid that you will leave me and go.
Anyone who learns Torah from one teacher
never sees a sign of blessing.
They left him and went to Rava.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the rule of דבי רבי ינאי inside a story about how it was applied.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning from only one teacher does not bring blessing, so the students went to learn from another teacher.

steps.title: For reasoning use many teachers; for the learned tradition one is better
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא limits the rule: it is about סברא. For גמרא, learning from one רב is better.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: this applies to reasoning. But for the learned tradition, learning from one teacher is better, so that...
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא narrows the rule he just taught. It only applies to one kind of learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of learning. סברא is understanding and reasoning, and hearing many teachers sharpens it. גמרא is the learned text and tradition itself, and for that one teacher is better. His reason begins with כי היכי ('so that') and continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: the learned tradition or text itself

steps.confusionAlert: Here גמרא does not mean the book of Talmud. It means the memorized tradition you receive from your teacher, as opposed to סברא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the rule against learning from one teacher is not absolute. It depends on what kind of learning you are doing.

phrases.english: He said to them: this applies to reasoning,
but for the learned tradition, from one teacher is better,
so that…

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule from the previous steps after the students left.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For reasoning, learn from many teachers. For the learned tradition itself, learning from one teacher is better.
